description: Expected input filenames and structures do not match the task’s specified inputs. The skill expects `topology.json`, `relationships.json`, and `route_leaks.json`, but the task provides `route.json`, `preferences.json`, and `local_pref.json` (relationship type weight). Following the skill as written would cause incorrect file loading/assumptions and may block analysis.

Solution-evaluation guidance conflicts with the task’s explicit resolution criteria. The skill claims Routing Intent and UDR can ‘resolve’ oscillation/leaks by overriding forwarding even if BGP oscillation or leak advertisements continue, but the task requires: (a) oscillation resolved only if the routing-preference cycle is broken, and (b) leak resolved only if hub1/hub2 stop advertising routes to each other via Virtual WAN. This mismatch would lead to false positives (marking solutions as resolved when they don’t meet the required conditions).

description: Hardcoded topology facts (specific ASNs and hub names) appear in normative reasoning text, encouraging brittle, non-input-derived logic. The skill references Virtual WAN as ASN 65001 and uses concrete hub ASNs/names (e.g., vhubvnet1 ASN 65002, vhubvnet2 ASN 65003) in explanatory sections, which can bias an agent toward hardcoding instead of deriving identifiers from the provided JSON inputs.

description: Overly strict input-validation rule: the skill requires relationship symmetry and declares the input invalid if symmetry checks fail. The task does not guarantee symmetric relationship encoding (and uses `local_pref.json` weights rather than an explicit bidirectional relationship map), so this rule can incorrectly halt or invalidate processing instead of performing best-effort detection.
